keyVerseText: But the Nethinims dwelt in Ophel: and Ziha and Gispa were over the Nethinims. Ophel: or, the tower
rootMeaning: The Hebrew term גִּשְׁפָּא (Gishpâʼ) is of uncertain derivation, with no clear root or etymology provided. Its meaning as a proper name rather than a common noun suggests it functions primarily as an identifier rather than a word with a definable root sense. The lexicon indicates it is a masculine personal name associated with an officer among the temple slaves, which highlights its role as a title or designation rather than a word with a literal meaning beyond the name itself.
usageInScripture: This word occurs only once in the entire Old Testament, appearing specifically in Nehemiah 11:21. It is translated simply as "and Gispa," indicating its use as a proper name rather than a descriptive term. The singular occurrence and consistent translation as a personal name reveal its function is limited to identifying an individual rather than conveying a broader conceptual meaning.
theologicalSignificance: Though Gishpâʼ appears only once as a personal name, its mention as an officer over the Nethinim—temple servants—underscores the importance of faithful leadership and service in the post-exilic community. This reminds believers of the value God places on those who serve in His house, even in roles that may seem minor or administrative. The presence of named individuals in Scripture, such as Gishpâʼ, affirms God's sovereign care over every member of His covenant people, highlighting the dignity and responsibility entrusted to His servants. It invites reflection on the faithfulness required in all areas of ministry and service within the body of Christ.
keyVerseReflection: Nehemiah 11:21 states, "But the Nethinims dwelt in Ophel: and Ziha and Gispa were over the Nethinims." The use of Gishpâʼ here identifies one of the leaders appointed to oversee the temple servants, emphasizing order and governance among God's people as they resettled Jerusalem. The inclusion of his name personalizes the historical record, showing that God’s work is carried out through named individuals who faithfully fulfill their roles. This verse highlights the importance of stewardship and leadership in the community of faith.
